Rashi on Gittin 58a:16:1.english: For the honor of Your mighty name - And where is Your might?

Rashi on Gittin 58a:17:1.english: Over Me and over you - for My name has been desecrated by this:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:18:1.hebrew: שוליא דנגרי הוה - לא היה רבו לתורה, אלא רבו לאומנות של נגרים:
Rashi on Gittin 58a:18:1.english: He was a carpenter’s apprentice - [His master] was not his Torah teacher, but rather his master in the craft of carpentry.

Rashi on Gittin 58a:1:1.hebrew: קצוצי תפילין - דפוסי תפילין חוץ מן הרצועה קרוי קציצה, כדאמרי' במסכת סוכה (דף כו:): "אוחז ברצועה ואינו אוחז בקציצה":
Rashi on Gittin 58a:1:1.english: Phylactery boxes - The casings of the phylacteries, excluding the strap, are called a ketzitzah, as we say in Tractate Sukkah (26b): "One holds [it] by the strap and does not hold [it] by the ketzitzah":

Rashi on Gittin 58a:21:1.english: Two wicks in one lamp - [This refers to] a married woman:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:22:1.english: They taught [only] - that his purchase is void:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:22:2.english: Only where they said to him - the owners [said this] to this [person] who purchased from a Sicarius:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:22:3.hebrew: לך חזק וקני - בחזקה, דכיון דדיבורא בעלמא הוא, איכא למימר "השני נוח לי":
Rashi on Gittin 58a:22:3.english: Go, take possession and acquire - [That is,] by taking possession, for since it is merely a verbal [statement], one can say [that the original owner's intention was], "The second one is easier for me [to deal with]":

Rashi on Gittin 58a:22:4.english: But - [with a bill of sale, i.e.,] if he wrote him a bill of sale in his name:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:22:5.hebrew: קני - דכולי האי לא הוה ליה למיעבד, אי לאו דזבנה ליה מכר גמור ומדעת:
Rashi on Gittin 58a:22:5.english: He acquires [it] - For he [the prior owner] would not have done all this [i.e., write a bill of sale], had he not sold it to him [as] a complete sale and willingly:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:22:6.hebrew: אחריות - דאי טרפו לה מיניה, לגבייה דמי ארעא:
Rashi on Gittin 58a:22:6.english: A guarantee - [Stating] that if [creditors] seize it from him, he may collect the value of the land from him:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:2:1.hebrew: דדרעא - מ' סאה, ודרישא — שהם גדולים, ד' בתים בכל קציצה — הוו ג' זימני מ' סאה. וא"ת ד'? לא היא, שבית אחד של זרוע גדול מאחד מבתי הראש, לפי שכאן כל ארבע פרשיות בבית אחד, ובשל ראש פרשה אחת בבית אחד. ומ"מ, דפוס של ראש — מתוך שצריך לחלק הבתים, ולהיות ריוח ביניהן, וקבועין על מושב אחד — הוצרך המושב להיות רחב, והוי על אחד שלשה שבזרוע:
Rashi on Gittin 58a:2:1.english: Of the arm - [That refers to] forty se'ah, and [those] of the head — which are large, [having] four compartments in each ketzitzah [tefillin box] — were three times forty se'ah. And if you say, [why not] four [times]? That is not so, because the single compartment of [the] arm [tefillin] is larger than one of the compartments of the head [tefillin], since here all four passages are in one compartment, whereas in [those] of the head, one passage is in each compartment. Nevertheless, [as for] the form of [the] head [tefillin] — since it is necessary to divide the compartments, and for there to be space between them, and they are set upon a single base — the base had to be wide, and [thus] it comes to three times [the size of] the one of the arm:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:3:1.english: Four kav - [this was] at the destruction of the First Temple:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:4:2.hebrew: שהיו מגנין את הפז ביופיין - והיינו "מסולאים", לשון "סולו לרוכב" (תהלים סח), "לא תסולה בכתם אופיר" — משובחין היו ביופיין מן הפז:
Rashi on Gittin 58a:4:2.english: That they would disgrace fine gold because of their beauty - And this is [the meaning of] "mesula'im," an expression [like] "extol [solu] Him who rides" (Psalms 68[:5]), [and] "it cannot be valued [lo tesuleh] with the gold of Ophir" [Job 28:16] — [meaning] they were superior in their beauty to fine gold:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:5:1.hebrew: בליוני דגושפנקי - צורות נאות שבחותמיהן, כדי שתתעברנה כנגדן:
Rashi on Gittin 58a:5:1.english: Images of a seal - Beautiful images on their signet rings, so that [their wives] would conceive opposite them:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:6:1.english: How far am I from that place - [meaning] that I have not [yet] reached learning that verse:

Rashi on Gittin 58a:6:3.english: Pusta and a half - A page [or column] and a half:

Tosafot on Gittin 58a:10:1.hebrew: כל ממון שפוסקין עליו - כי איכא סכנת נפשות, פודין שבויין יותר על כדי דמיהן, כדאמרינן בפרק השולח (לעיל גיטין דף מד.) גבי מוכר עצמו ואת בניו לעובדי כוכבים; כ"ש הכא דאיכא קטלא. אי נמי, משום דמופלג בחכמה היה:
Tosafot on Gittin 58a:10:1.english: Whatever money they set for him - When there is danger to life, we ransom captives for more than their value, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Hasholeach (above, Gittin 44a) regarding one who sells himself and his children to idolaters; all the more so here, where there is [danger of] killing. Alternatively, [it was permitted] because he was outstanding in wisdom:

Tosafot on Gittin 58a:22:1.hebrew: אבל בשטר קנה - אאשה נמי קאי, כדמוכח בסמוך. והא דאמר בפרק מי שהיה נשוי (כתובות דף צה.): "כתב לראשון ולא חתמה לו, ולשני וחתמה לו — איבדה כתובתה", משמע דבחד לוקח יכולה לומר "נחת רוח עשיתי לבעלי" — התם כשחתמה על שטר של בעלה, והכא כשכתבה שטר בפני עצמה. ועוד, ד"חתמה" דהתם — שנתרצית במכירת הבעל, או שמחלה לו השעבוד; אבל הכא, כשכתבה שטר מכירה שהיא מוכרת לו. ולמאי דמפרש ה"ר אליעזר משנז"א, דרב ושמואל פליגי הכא ב"אחריות טעות סופר הוא" — דשמואל לטעמיה, דאמר בפ"ק דב"מ (דף יד.) דאחריות לאו טעות סופר הוא בשטרי מקח וממכר, ורב סבר אחריות ט"ס הוא, ובסתם שטר ככתבה לו אחריות דמי — וההיא דכתובות כשפירשה דלא קבלה אחריות מידי:
Tosafot on Gittin 58a:22:1.english: But with a bill [of sale], he acquires [it] - [This] also refers to a wife, as is proven shortly [in the Gemara]. And as for that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehaya Nasui (Ketubot 95a): "[If a husband] wrote [a deed of sale] to a first [buyer] and [his wife] did not sign for him, and [then he sold] to a second [buyer] and she signed for him, she has lost her ketubah," which implies that in the case of a single buyer she can say, "I did it to please my husband" — there [it is speaking of a case] where she signed on her husband's bill [of sale], whereas here [it is speaking of a case] where she wrote a bill [of sale] on her own. And furthermore, "she signed" there [means] that she consented to the husband's sale or that she waived the lien for him, whereas here [it is speaking of a case] where she wrote a bill of sale [stating] that she is selling [it] to him. And according to what Rabbi Eliezer of Sens explains — that Rav and Shmuel disagree here regarding [whether the omission of] a guarantee is a scribal error, for Shmuel follows his own reasoning, as he says in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (14a) that [the omission of] a guarantee is not a scribal error in bills of purchase and sale, whereas Rav holds that [the omission of] a guarantee is a scribal error, and in an unspecified bill [of sale] it is as though she wrote him a guarantee — that [case] in Ketubot [is speaking of a case] where she explicitly stated that she did not accept any guarantee:
